slides.say: A, B and C represent digits, and A is bigger than C, which is bigger than zero. Which of the following could be the value of A B C minus C B A?

slides: We take the three-digit number A B C and subtract C B A, the same digits in reverse order. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, writing their place values, and then trying numbers.

slides.say: [short pause] Let's start with the place values. A B C is a hundred A plus ten B plus C. C B A is a hundred C plus ten B plus A. Subtract the second from the first. The ten B parts cancel because B is in the same place in both numbers. The A parts leave ninety-nine A, and the C parts leave minus ninety-nine C.
at: A B C is a hundred A

slides.say: So the result is ninety-nine times the whole bracket, A minus C. It must be a multiple of ninety-nine.

Now check the answer choices as possible results. Three-digit multiples of ninety-nine have nine in the middle, and their first and last digits add to nine. A hundred ninety-eight, two hundred ninety-seven, and three hundred ninety-six follow that pattern. Four hundred fifty-nine has five in the middle, so it's out. Four hundred eighty-four has eight in the middle, so it's out. Five hundred forty has four in the middle, so it's out too.
Four hundred ninety-five has nine in the middle, and four plus five is nine. It is ninety-nine times five. It's the only choice left, so choice number three is our answer.
at: choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's build an example. The check for multiples of ninety-nine only ruled out choices. It doesn't show that four hundred ninety-five can really be the difference, because A and C must be digits, with A bigger than C and C bigger than zero. The question asks what could be the value, so one example that satisfies every given is enough. We found that the difference is ninety-nine times the whole bracket, A minus C. Four hundred ninety-five is ninety-nine times five, so we need A minus C is five. An easy pair is A is six and C is one. Six minus one is five.
at: Four hundred ninety-five is ninety-nine times five

slides.say: B cancels in the subtraction, so use an easy digit, two. That gives six hundred twenty-one and its reversal, a hundred twenty-six. A is six and C is one, so A is greater than C and C is not zero. Six hundred twenty-one minus a hundred twenty-six: taking away a hundred twenty-one leaves five hundred, and five more leaves four hundred ninety-five. It fits every given, so choice number three is our answer. We can stop without trying more digit pairs. Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: choice number three is our answer
